item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback! I understand why you believe this wouldn’t initially be considered anomalous, but I still feel it warrants an EX designation. Why I believe that this would be considered an EX is because of its close relation to other anomalous activity. In addition, it was thought to possibly harbor cognitohazardous or otherwise mind-affecting properties when it was first discovered.

The logs themselves support the idea of it being at least created by an anomalous humanoid involved with a known GoI. Things like this have been used in other Explained SCPs like SCP-1094-EX where the only perceived anomalous property was that it looked like a big eyeball. To hopefully clear this up, I’ve added that the object class for the posters was pending, similarly to 1094-EX. Again, thanks for the clear and concise feedback, I really do appreciate it.

item.title: Re: hmmm...
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for your critique! I've decided to remove the idea of the item being previously deemed anomalous, which includes the removal of the archived procedures. I added and changed a small amount of the procedures to try and express that 1. Not everyone who sees the anomaly immediately thinks they have the disease which I've expressed in the recovery and 2. that people who think they have the disease are people who are in an environment where things are anomalous. In the recovery, people at the hospital only reported that the posters existed, not that they had the disease. The only ones who have claimed to be affected so far are those in a setting where it could be anomalous for all they know.

As for the chat logs, I only meant for this to be a brief glimpse into their world. A quick little distraction so that Toaster could move apartments without being hassled by the Foundation. I feel that extending the logs would only make the article more drawn out.

Again, your advice was really helpful and I'm happy that you enjoyed the article!

item.title: hmmm...
item.content:encoded:
I'll stuff my thoughts on the collapsible below.

+ My thoughts
- Hide my thoughts

First off, I think your clinical tone is spot on, and there's not much left to me to complain about. The sentences are clear, and the overall structure of the article has been pulled off well. Also, the image is pretty nice, so good job on that. Now, to the whole…

I'm not really sure of what the point of the anomaly is? Sure, ToasterDoot created them to cause trouble to the Foundation, but even then I didn't understand the reasoning behind it previously cataloging them as anomalous. People apparently thought that seeing them caused unrelated symptoms? I don't think there's enough buildup on that, and it should be explained further.

The chat conversation feels realistic to me, and their personalities are clearly presented, but it's too short to make me care about the characters and their relationships. I felt like I only catched a brief glimpse of a bigger article, and I don't really understand what exactly is going on in the lives of the GAW group; I'm not sure on how to remedy that, but maybe extending the logs and including further explanation could help with it?

I'm ultimately no-voting here. I personally think you've took a hold of a good concept basis here, and you've included good imagery, but the downside I see is its vagueness and lack of a build-up.
